title: Invertibility of the normalized derived slice comparison mate
statement: Let $\mathcal D$ and $\mathcal C$ be small categories with Grothendieck topologies $K$ and $J$, let $u:\mathcal D\to\mathcal C$ be continuous, let $R$ and $S$ be sheaves of commutative rings on them, and let $a:R\to u_*S$ be a sheaf ring map. Suppose $u^{-1}$ on sheaves of sets preserves finite limits. Use module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] with chosen localization universes. For a continuous morphism of small ringed sites with left exact inverse image, fix an object V, its localized morphism, and any normalized global and localized derived adjunction presentations [def-weil-pbc-ringed-slice-derived-data]. Suppose beta is a natural isomorphism from restriction after derived direct image to local derived direct image after restriction, whose square with the right-derived units and the termwise restriction factorizations commutes on every complex. Then its inverse adjunction mate is invertible. No section localization assertion is part of this lemma.

proof.text: Use left-derived uniqueness to compare the supplied derived images with the normalized construction. Their counits are therefore invertible on flat-term K-flat complexes. Restriction preserves K-flatness and flatness of terms.

Specialize the ordinary inverse-adjunct identity to the unit. The categorical mate unit identity, the two normalized derived Hom formulas, normalization of beta and naturality of the restriction factorization identify the mate followed by the global counit with the local counit followed by Q of the ordinary pullback comparison. On a flat-term K-flat representative every other factor is invertible, hence so is the mate.

Resolve a complex representative of every derived object by a flat-term K-flat complex. Naturality along the inverted resolution map transfers invertibility of the mate component from this representative to the object. Componentwise invertibility gives invertibility of the natural transformation.
